subject: Back-transforming data for plotting detection probabilities

messages.author: 48e53ec4949972f6
messages.subject: Back-transforming data for plotting detection probabilities
parts:
Hello,

I am new to using unmarked and still trying to figure out how to use the basic functions. I have a question regarding plotting detection curves with z-standardized data. I have attached an image of the plot I made using the standardized data and my code below. My question is this: how do I plot the probability of detection using the unstandardized data? 

newdata.1<-data.frame(turb=seq(-0.5,10,by=0.1))
fm2.p<-predict(fm2,type="det",newdata=newdata.1,appendData=TRUE)
plot(Predicted ~ turb, fm2.p, type="l", ylim=c(0,1),
            xlab="Turbidity (FTU)",
            ylab="Probability of Detection")
lines(lower ~ turb, fm2.p, type="l", col=gray(0.5))
lines(upper ~ turb, fm2.p, type="l", col=gray(0.5))

I found code on the online webinar (moduleOCC.r) that i tried but it just basically changes the x-axis back to the original data (see below and second attached image).Is there something I am missing? Is this how it is supposed to be done? Because my original un-standardized data does not go below zero. The sampling covariate in question here is turbidity (data is from an eDNA study) and turbidity units (FTU) do not go below zero. Am i supposed to be back-transforming the original data somehow, not just changing the axes?

plot(Predicted ~ turb, fm2.p, type="l", ylim=c(0,1),
              xlab="Turbidity (FTU)",
              ylab="Probability of Detection")
xticks <- 1:10
xlabs <- xticks*turb.sd + turb.mean
axis(1, at=xticks, labels=round(xlabs, 1))
lines(lower ~ turb,fm2.p , type="l", col=gray(0.5))
lines(upper ~ turb, fm2.p, type="l", col=gray(0.5))


Also, does anyone have any suggestions on how to make these same plots using ggplot2? I like the look of plots in that package better...but for now have just been using the basic plot() function.


Thank you for your time and help!

messages.author: dc8b4131b39a099f
messages.subject: Re: Back-transforming data for plotting detection probabilities
parts:
Hi Sean. Here is some old code I wrote to standardize covariate values for model fitting and then backtransform them for plotting predictions. It's not pretty but maybe it will be helpful.

umf=csvToUMF("GRSP veg.csv",long=FALSE,type="unmarkedFramePCount")

sc=siteCovs(umf)
sc[,6:12]=scale(sc[,6:12])
siteCovs(umf)=sc

Bare=pcount(~obs+visit ~BARE+offset(log(AREA)),mixture="ZIP",umf)

DF=data.frame(BARE=seq(-0.5,5,0.5),AREA=10)
pred=predict(Bare,type="state",newdata=DF,backTran=FALSE,appendData=FALSE)
abun=exp(pred$Predicted)
LCL=exp(pred$Predicted-(pred$SE*1.435))
UCL=exp(pred$Predicted+(pred$SE*1.435))
av=mean(data$BARE)
stdv=sd(data$BARE)
xval=data.frame(BARE=seq(-0.5,5,0.5)*stdv+av)
matrix(data=c(LCL,abun,UCL),ncol=3,dimnames=list(xval$BARE))
